classes.name: Minn\Admin\ActivityChart
classes.doc:
The overview's activity chart: published posts and pages plus every
comment, counted per bar. A window over 45 days is drawn in weeks,
anything shorter in days; each bar carries the (from, to] GMT bounds
the drill-down asks for.

methods.name: bars
methods.doc: The bars for a window of days, counted from the database.
shapes: @return list<array{label: string, value: int, from: string, to: string}>

methods.name: bucket
methods.doc:
GMT stamps into bars, oldest first. Labels are site-local: the day
for daily bars, "Week of" the bar's first day for weekly ones.
shapes: @return list<array{label: string, value: int, from: string, to: string}>

classes.name: Minn\Admin\ActivityFeed
classes.doc:
What happened lately, as the overview and the bell tell it: the caller's
own recent posts and the latest comments, and the events behind one
chart bar. Also the visibility rule every comment row is put through.

methods.name: recent
methods.doc:
The overview's four most recent items, times already worded ("2 hours ago").

Oracle-caught quirk: the reference's recent-activity query runs with a
multi-type post_type plus perm=editable, and on that combination it
restricts EVERY status to post_author = caller, admins included,
published posts included. Authorless posts appear for nobody. The
engine reproduces the observed behavior, not the intent.

methods.name: between
methods.doc:
The events behind one chart bar, (from, to] GMT, newest first. Post
rows decode the RAW stored title; comment rows decode the texturized
one (the reference's asymmetry, kept).

methods.name: commentVisible
methods.doc: May this caller see a comment row that names its post?

methods.name: postTitle
methods.doc: A post's stored title, empty when the post is gone.

methods.name: displayName
methods.doc: A user's display name, empty when the user is gone.

methods.name: ownPosts
methods.doc: The caller's own posts, merged from a by-modified and a by-date window.

shell and assets from. Minn Admin is MIT, so reading its files is fine.

Whether the site has switched Minn Admin off: its plugin folder is in

classes.name: Minn\Admin\AppController

Serves Minn Admin from the engine: the path-routed shell (every
sub-path renders the same page), the app's assets, and the one
admin-ajax action app.js uses to refresh its nonce.

The shell reproduces the structure of Minn Admin's own template.php

classes.name: Minn\Admin\Appearance
classes.doc:
A person's Minn Admin appearance: the colour scheme and its custom
token maps, stored where the app stores them (user meta
minn_admin_appearance, a serialized array) so the choice survives an
eject. The two WordPress-era switches, "Minn is the default admin" and
"Minn admin bar on the site", are always on here: there is no other
admin and no other bar, so the engine reports them true and ignores
writes to them.

constants.doc: Scheme slots in the order the app lists them.

constants.name: BASE
constants.doc: The app's own Minn tokens, the fill for incomplete custom maps.

shapes: @return array{scheme: string, custom: array, defaultAdmin: bool, frontBar: bool}

methods.doc: Merges the given keys over the stored map and writes it back; returns the normalised result.

methods.name: normalise
methods.doc: The appearance with every field valid and every missing one defaulted.

methods.name: hex
methods.doc: #rgb or #rrggbb to lowercase #rrggbb, or '' for anything else.

methods.doc:
What the app may show, each key a capability the reference gates the
same view on. The commerce caps mirror the plugin's own conditions:

What Minn Admin's own boot_payload() computes when the plugin runs as
code on the runtime, so the app boots with the same keys on both

the app to a wp-admin page the engine does not have.

methods.doc:
The reference serves the app shell from the home query, so the global
post is the newest post while the payload is built; the comments
feature check reads it through the comments_open filter (a site that
closes comments on old posts reports the feature off when its newest
post is old).

What Minn Admin's own adapters contribute when the plugin runs as code
on the runtime: plugin surfaces (Tools), editor panels, design
sources, editor commands, block forms. Absent, the app's fallbacks apply.

The language picker's markup. English always leads the list and carries the
empty value, because "no locale" and "American English" are the same choice.
When the picker also offers what could be downloaded, the two halves split
into named groups; otherwise every option sits in one flat list.

The attribute order is not tidy and is not ours to tidy: the English option
carries `data-installed` before `selected`, an installed translation carries
it after, and themes and plugins have been matching on that markup for
years.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\Packages
classes.doc:
Putting themes and extensions on disk. Themes come from wordpress.org
(block themes render on the engine) or an uploaded zip; extensions come
from an uploaded zip or a URL, and must carry a minn.json: a WordPress
plugin would install but never run, so it is refused with the reason.
Every archive is unpacked through one guarded routine: exactly one
top-level folder that is a plain name (never "." or ".."), no absolute
or dotted paths, no symbolic links, bounded entry count and size, the
folder's identity checked and its destination proven to be a direct
child of the kind's directory before it is moved into place. Removal
proves the same containment before anything is deleted.

classes.name: Minn\Admin\Translations
classes.doc:
Languages for the admin. A person's locale is their `locale` user meta,
else the site's WPLANG, else en_US, exactly as the reference resolves it.
The app translates itself from a map of its source strings, read from the
JED catalogs Minn Admin's language packs install under
wp-content/languages/plugins (the bundle's own languages folder is the
fallback). Installing a pack fetches the release asset the bundle's
manifest names for that locale, checks its hash, and unpacks only that
locale's files, so an eject leaves the files WordPress would have written.

methods.doc: The locale a person reads the admin in.

methods.name: siteLocale

methods.doc: Whether a locale reads right to left.

methods.doc:
The app's translation map for a locale: source string => translation,
or the plural forms as a list. Later folders win, so the installed
pack lands over the bundle's fallback.

installedCodes

classes.name: Minn\Admin\Updates
classes.doc:
Update offers from wordpress.org for the site's plugins and themes: the
directory's update-check endpoints asked with the installed headers, the
answer kept in the minn_updates option (JSON) for twelve hours, and the
offers applied by downloading the release archive through the one
package unpacker. A plugin or theme the directory does not know keeps
its folder untouched and is never offered anything. The per-item
auto-update lists are the site's own auto_update_plugins and
auto_update_themes options, in the shape the app already reads.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: The stored answer, refreshed when older than the TTL or absent.

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Asks wordpress.org now, whatever the cache says, and keeps the answer.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: Asks the directory now and stores the answer.

methods.name: pluginOffers
methods.doc: Plugin file => offered version, only where the installed version is older. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: themeOffers
methods.doc: Stylesheet => offered version. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: pluginMeta
methods.doc: Plugin file => slug, icon, directory URL, for every plugin the directory knows. @return array<string, array{slug: string, icon: string, url: string}>
shapes: @return array<string, array{slug: string, icon: string, url: string}>

methods.name: themeOnDirectory
methods.doc: Whether wordpress.org knows this theme.

methods.name: updatePlugin
methods.doc: Applies the offer for one plugin file; returns the installed version afterwards.

methods.name: updateTheme
methods.doc: Updates one theme to its offer; the new version.

methods.name: auto
methods.doc: The auto-update list for plugins or themes, trimmed to what is installed. @return list<string>

methods.name: enableAuto
methods.doc: Turns auto-updates on or off for one plugin or theme.
shapes: @return list<string> the list after the change

methods.name: runAuto
methods.doc: Applies every offer on the auto-update lists; returns what was updated. @return list<string>

methods.name: pluginVersions

methods.name: pluginNames

methods.name: themeHeaders

Stores an auto-update list, kept to assets that exist; the asset being

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Fetches and unpacks an offer's package. Every redirect hop must stay
on the wordpress.org download host, and the archive's SHA-256 is kept
under "archives" in the state so an audit can ask what code arrived.

methods.name: consume
methods.doc: An applied offer moves to the current bucket so the next read agrees with the folder.

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The directory answers an empty bucket as a list; a map either way.

classes.doc:
The boot burst of minn-admin/v1: the bell feed and its read marker, the
core status, and the one-round-trip boot-status the app starts from.
Every route sits behind the same capability floor (edit_posts) the
plugin declares.

methods.name: notificationsRead
methods.doc: Body {id} marks one read; {} marks all read.

methods.name: core
methods.doc: The core status.

methods.name: bootStatus
methods.doc:
The app's one-round-trip boot burst. Absent sections are the
contract's own fallback: the client loads a missing section
standalone. The engine serves what it can honestly answer and omits
the plugin-inventory sections it has no installation for.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\ApplicationPasswords
classes.doc:
Application passwords as the reference stores them: a serialized list in
the user's _application_passwords meta, each entry uuid, app_id, name,
password (a hash), created, last_used, last_ip. New passwords are 24
characters shown in groups of four; the stored hash is phpass, which the
reference verifies too, so a password made here survives a switch back.
A hash the reference made with its own fast scheme cannot be verified here.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every application password of a user, as stored records without the hash's plain text.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: One record by uuid, or null.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Mints a password, stores its hash, and returns the record with the plain text once.
shapes: @return array{0: array<string, mixed>, 1: string} the stored record and the one-time plaintext

methods.name: rename
methods.doc: Renames one password; null when the uuid is unknown.

methods.name: touch
methods.doc: Records a use: the time and the address it came from.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes one password and returns its record; null when unknown.

methods.name: deleteAll
methods.doc: Removes every application password of a user and returns how many.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: The record a plaintext (spaces ignored) unlocks for the user, or null.

methods.name: generate
methods.doc: Twenty-four letters and digits.

methods.name: chunked
methods.doc: The plaintext as shown once: groups of four, space separated.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\AuthCookies
classes.doc:
The three cookies a sign-in sets: the auth cookie on the admin and
plugins paths (the secure variant over HTTPS, keyed off that scheme's
salt) and the logged_in cookie on the site root, which is the one REST
reads. Every value shares the username|expiration|token|hmac shape.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The hash suffixed onto every cookie name: md5 of the siteurl option.

methods.name: attach
methods.signature: attach(Minn\Http\Response $response, Minn\Content\UserRecord $user, int $expiration, string $token, bool $secure, bool $persistent = false): Minn\Http\Response
methods.doc: A non-persistent sign-in keeps the server expiry but sends session cookies the browser drops on close.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: The response with every sign-in cookie expired.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc: A cookie value under any scheme's salt (auth, secure_auth, logged_in).

classes.name: Minn\Auth\AuthFailure
classes.doc:
Why a request is not authenticated, as the reference's error code: a
missing or invalid cookie is rest_not_logged_in (the request is simply
anonymous); a good cookie with a bad nonce is rest_cookie_invalid_nonce.

methods.name: notLoggedIn
methods.doc: No usable session.

methods.name: invalidNonce
methods.doc: A session whose nonce did not verify.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Authenticated
classes.doc: A validated session: the user row and the raw session token behind it.

shapes: @param array<string, mixed>|null $applicationPassword the record that authenticated this call, when Basic auth did

params.name: applicationPassword
params.doc: the record that authenticated this call, when Basic auth did

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The signed-in user's id.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Authenticator
classes.doc:
Resolves the current user two ways. A page load carries the cookie alone;
a REST call must also carry a nonce bound to the same session.

constants.name: NOBODY
constants.doc: A real hash of a password nobody knows, checked against when the user does not exist so the answer takes as long either way.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: An authenticator over the shared database door.

methods.name: session
methods.doc: The session the cookie jar carries, or why there is none.

methods.name: rest
methods.doc: The session for a REST call: the cookie, then the nonce.

methods.name: restFromRequest
methods.doc:
A REST caller: the cookie session with its nonce first; failing that,
HTTP Basic credentials carrying an application password, which need no
nonce. A wrong Basic pair is reported as not logged in.

methods.name: applicationPassword
methods.doc: The user an Authorization: Basic header's application password unlocks, with the use recorded.

methods.name: applicationPasswordsAvailable
methods.doc: Application passwords need HTTPS, unless plugin code says otherwise through the reference's filter.

methods.name: applicationPasswordsAvailableFor
methods.doc: Whether Basic auth may sign this user in; the runtime's filter has the last word.

methods.name: login
methods.doc: Username and password to a user row; no session is created here.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Capabilities
classes.doc:
The capability engine: a user's roles from {prefix}capabilities usermeta,
the primitives those roles grant, and the meta-capability mapping for
edit_post, delete_post, and read_post.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: The capability engine over the shared database door.

methods.name: roles
methods.doc: The role definitions.

methods.name: rolesOf
methods.doc: The role slugs a user holds.

methods.name: primitivesOf
methods.doc: Every primitive capability a user holds through their roles.
shapes: @return array<string, true> the union of primitives the user's roles grant

methods.name: can
methods.doc: Does the user hold every primitive the (possibly meta) capability maps to?

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The primitives a capability requires, all of which must be held.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Cookie
classes.doc:
The logged_in auth cookie: username|expiration|token|hmac, with
key  = HMAC-md5(username|fragment|expiration|token, logged_in salt)
hmac = HMAC-sha256(username|expiration|token, key)
and the session live in the user's session_tokens store.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: The cookie name this site uses: a hash of the siteurl option.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc: A sign-in cookie value for a user, expiry, and session token.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc: The session a cookie value proves, or null when any part fails.

methods.name: fromJar
methods.doc:
The logged_in cookie from a request's cookie jar: the canonical name
first, then any logged_in cookie, since tooling may send a name
derived from a different host.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\LoginThrottle
classes.doc:
Failed sign-ins per address, so a password guesser meets a wall: twenty
failures in fifteen minutes and the address waits out the window. The
counters live in the options table (autoload off), one row per address,
as "window start:count"; a successful sign-in clears the row.

methods.name: retryAfter
methods.doc: Seconds the address must wait, or null when it may try.

methods.name: recordFailure
methods.doc: Counts one failed sign-in from an address within the current window.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets an address's failures.

methods.name: read
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: int} window start and failure count

methods.name: prune
methods.doc: Rows whose window has passed are dead weight; drop them now and then.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Nonce
classes.doc:
The wp_rest nonce: ten characters of HMAC-md5(tick|wp_rest|uid|token)
under the nonce salt, accepted for the current tick and the one before.

methods.name: tick
methods.doc: The current half-life tick a nonce is bound to.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: A wp_rest nonce for a user and session token at the current tick.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a nonce is valid at this tick or the one before.

methods.name: at
methods.doc: The nonce for a given tick.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Password
classes.doc:
The stored password scheme. A modern "$wp$2y$..." value is bcrypt over
base64(HMAC-sha384(password, "wp-sha384")); a bare "$2y$" value is plain
bcrypt. Legacy phpass "$P$" hashes are not verified.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a stored hash of either scheme.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A stored hash in the modern scheme: "$wp" plus bcrypt over the pre-hash.

methods.name: fragment
methods.doc:
The four characters of the hash the cookie key is derived from: the
LAST four for a "$wp$" hash, offset 8 for legacy phpass. Getting this
wrong yields a cookie that verifies nowhere while every other check
passes, so both branches are pinned by the auth suite.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PasswordReset
classes.doc:
Password reset keys in the reference's storage shape: user_activation_key
holds "time:hash", the key itself travels in the email link and is good
for a day. The hash is the engine's own ($minn$ over the nonce salt); a
key the reference issued ($generic$) is not readable here, so it is
refused and the reader asks for a fresh link.

methods.name: issue
methods.doc: Mints a key, stores its hash, returns the key for the link.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: True when the key matches the stored hash and has not expired.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: "valid", "expired" (a matching key past its day), or "invalid".

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets a user's reset key.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Phpass
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ($P$), from Openwall's public description of the
scheme: a log2 iteration count, an eight-character salt, and an iterated
MD5 in phpass's own base-64 alphabet. The reference still verifies these
for application passwords, which makes them the portable choice.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A portable phpass hash of a password.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a portable phpass hash.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc: phpass's base-64: 6 bits at a time, low bits first, no padding.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PortableHash
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ("$P$"), the shape the reference stores in
the post-password cookie: an iteration count character, an eight
character salt, and MD5 iterated over salt and password, encoded in
phpass's own base64 alphabet. Implemented from the published algorithm
so cookies are accepted in both directions.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The reference's cookies carry 2^13 iterations; it accepts nothing weaker.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: Whether a password matches a portable hash from the published algorithm.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Roles
classes.doc:
Role definitions from the site's {prefix}user_roles option, parsed by a
bounded scan of the serialized blob, with the seeded contract copy as the
fallback for a fresh install.

methods.name: level
methods.doc: The wp_user_level stored beside the capabilities meta.

methods.name: serializeSingle
methods.doc: The {role: true} capabilities meta in its serialized form.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Drops the parsed map so the next read sees a rewritten option.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every role with its name and capabilities, from the option or the shipped defaults.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
Each role is a string key over a two-entry array of "name" and
"capabilities"; the capabilities map is {cap: bool}. Null when the
blob has another shape, so the caller can fall back.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Salts
classes.doc:
The site's own secret material, read from the constants wp-config.php
defines, so the engine keys off exactly what the install used.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: True when every key and salt is defined and none is the installer's placeholder.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The key and salt of a scheme joined, as the reference feeds them to its HMACs.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: HMAC-md5 under the scheme's salt: the primitive every cookie and nonce is built from.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Sessions
classes.doc:
The session_tokens usermeta store: {sha256(token): {expiration, ip, ua,
login}}. Read by a bounded scan of the serialized blob and written by
serializing it ourselves, so stored data is never executed.

methods.name: generateToken
methods.doc: A 43-character token; only sha256(token) is ever stored or compared.

methods.name: isLive
methods.doc: Whether a session token is still stored and unexpired for a user.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a session, pruning expired ones, and returns the raw token.

methods.name: destroyAll
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user (a password change).

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Removes one session; true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyKey
methods.doc: Removes the session stored under a key (the sha256 of its token); true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyOthers
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user except the one stored under the given key.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: Every stored session of a user, keyed by token hash.
shapes: @return array<string, array{expiration: int, ip: string, ua: string, login: int}>

methods.name: serialize
methods.doc: The map in PHP's serialized form, entry keys in the order given.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\SignIn
classes.doc:
The door itself: what a sign-in surface needs beyond checking a
password. Sessions are minted here, the three cookies ride out on the
response, and the failure counter behind the throttle is kept in one
place with the session store and the cookie jar it protects.

methods.name: retryAfter
methods.doc: Seconds this address must wait before another attempt, or null when it may try now.

methods.name: recordFailure
methods.doc: Counts one failed attempt from an address.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The cookie-name hash the sign-in cookies, the postpass cookie, and the reset cookie share.

methods.name: establish
methods.doc: Signs a user in for two days: a new session, and the response with the cookies attached for the browser session.

methods.name: remember
methods.doc: Signs a user in for fourteen days, the cookies kept past the browser session: "remember me", and the one-time login link.

methods.name: end
methods.doc: Ends one session and clears the cookies from the response.

methods.name: endAll
methods.doc: Ends every session of a user (a password reset) and clears the cookies from the response.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: The response with the sign-in cookies cleared.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: A session longer than the two-day default is one to keep past the browser session, as the reference's remember-me does.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\TypeCapabilities

The capability names a post type's permissions are built from. Posts and
pages own their families (edit_posts, edit_others_pages, ...). Navigation
menus fold every one of them onto edit_theme_options, which is why an
editor may read a menu and only an administrator may change one; the
reference's own registration says the same thing.

constants.doc: Types whose whole cap family collapses to a single name.

methods.doc: A cap name built from the post/page family, folded when the type folds.

methods.name: plural
methods.doc: The capability stem of a type: pages for page, posts for everything else.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc: The edit capability of a type.

methods.name: editOthers
methods.doc: The edit-others capability of a type.

methods.name: publish
methods.doc: The publish capability of a type.

methods.name: readPrivate

One parsed block. A null name is freeform HTML between blocks. The
innerContent list holds the block's own HTML chunks in order, with a
null placeholder wherever an inner block sits.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\BlockName

Per-block element styles (style.elements in a block's attributes, the

Blocks whose colour support has no element slots: their stored

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\ImageTags
classes.doc: The attributes the reference adds to an that carries a wp-image-{id} class: loading, decoding, width and height (prepended, in that order), and srcset plus sizes (appended). The srcset lists the displayed size first, then every same-ratio size in stored order, then the original.

shapes: @param Closure(): bool $front whether the images are on a front-end page, where the loading budget applies

params.name: front
params.doc: whether the images are on a front-end page, where the loading budget applies

methods.name: enrich
methods.doc: Rewrites every wp-image-* in a fragment; other images pass through.

methods.name: enrichGallery
methods.doc: The same for a gallery: every image also carries its data-id.

methods.name: enrichPlugin
methods.doc: The same for a plugin block's output, where the reference adds no sizes="auto".

methods.name: featured
methods.doc:
A post's featured image at full size, in the reference's attribute
order (dimensions, source, class, alt, style, then the loading
attributes and the srcset). Empty when the attachment has no file.

methods.name: loadingPrefix
methods.doc:
On a page the first big-enough content image is fetched eagerly with
high priority, the next few are eager, and the rest lazy; only lazy
images carry the "auto" sizes hint. In a REST response every image is
lazy.

methods.name: minimumPriorityPixels
methods.doc: The area an image must cover before it is worth fetching first.

methods.name: srcsetAttributes
methods.signature: srcsetAttributes(array $candidates, int $width, bool $auto, int $attachmentId = 0, array $meta = array ( ), string $src = '', int $height = 0): string
methods.doc:
A srcset needs a choice: one candidate yields no srcset and no sizes.
With the runtime up, plugin code filters the candidates and the sizes
hint the way the reference lets it (wp_calculate_image_srcset,
wp_calculate_image_sizes).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Layout
classes.doc:
The layout-support classes the reference adds at render time. Every
container carries is-layout-{type} and {block}-is-layout-{type}; flex and
grid layouts with rules of their own also carry a wp-container-* class
whose suffix names their generated stylesheet.

That suffix is a digest the engine cannot reproduce (its inputs are not
observable), so the engine derives its own deterministic suffix from the
layout attributes. Same shape, different value: recorded in the contract,
and the parity suites normalise it.

constants.name: ALWAYS_CONTAINER
constants.doc: Blocks the reference always gives a numbered container, whether or not their layout carries rules.

properties.name: rootPaddingAware
properties.doc: Whether the active theme opts into root-padding-aware alignments (theme.json settings.useRootPaddingAwareAlignments).

methods.name: rootPaddingAware
methods.doc: Whether the theme uses root padding-aware alignments.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The layout classes a block's wrapper carries.

methods.name: declarations
methods.doc: The declarations behind a container class, in the reference's order.

methods.name: hasRules
methods.doc: A container stylesheet exists only when the layout declares something the defaults do not.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Parser
classes.doc:
Parses block markup into a tree. The grammar is the delimiter comment:
an opener with optional JSON attributes, a closer, or a self-closing
void block; a name without a namespace is core/. Anything outside a
block is a freeform block that renders as-is.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: Block markup as a tree of blocks.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Whether serialized content carries a block by name; a bare name means core/, and core blocks are also found by their short delimiter.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\QueryVars
classes.doc: The query variables a Query Loop block's context asks for, the way the reference's query block builds them.

shapes: @param list<int> $sticky the site's sticky post ids

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\RenderState
classes.doc:
Per-request rendering state, owned by the renderer. The reference numbers
galleries, style variations, and search inputs from ONE counter that runs
across every block rendered in the request (a list response keeps
counting from post to post), so the counter lives here, not on any block.
Leaf helpers with no renderer in hand reach it through current().

properties.name: pendingElements
properties.doc: the element class claimed for the dynamic block being rendered, until its wrapper takes it

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The request's state: the renderer's own once one exists, else a fresh one that the first renderer adopts.

methods.name: adopt
methods.doc: Makes this the request's state, the one current() answers with.

methods.name: nextId
methods.doc: The next per-request counter value.

methods.name: nextImage
methods.doc: Content images seen so far in this page, for the loading rules.

methods.name: refundImages
methods.doc:
Images a plugin's block filter removed from the page give their budget
back, so the next image still counts as if the hidden ones never rendered.

methods.name: claimPriority
methods.doc: True once, for the image that gets fetchpriority="high".

methods.name: recordContainer
methods.doc: A container stylesheet this page needs: the class and its declarations.

methods.name: containers
methods.doc: The layout containers rendering discovered.

methods.name: recordBlock
methods.doc: Every block name the page rendered; the stylesheet prints block styles for these only.

methods.name: blocks
methods.doc: The block names rendering met.

methods.name: recordVariation
methods.doc: Notes a style variation instance for the stylesheet.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc: The style variations rendering met.

methods.name: nextElements
methods.doc: The next wp-elements-N class; the reference numbers these apart from the shared counter.

methods.name: uniqueLabel
methods.doc: A navigation's aria-label: the label itself the first time, then "label N" for repeats.

methods.name: enterNavigation
methods.doc:
A page list renders plain on its own and takes the navigation block's
item classes, submenu toggles, and interactivity only while it sits
inside one, so the navigation block marks the span it owns.

methods.name: leaveNavigation
methods.doc: Leaves a navigation block.

methods.name: inNavigation
methods.doc: Whether rendering is inside a navigation block.

methods.name: enter
methods.doc: Marks a nested source as being rendered; false when it is already open (a cycle).

methods.name: leave

methods.name: descend
methods.doc: True while the block tree is shallower than the cap; deeper blocks render as nothing.

methods.name: ascend
methods.doc: Leaves one nesting level.

methods.name: depth
methods.doc: How deep the block tree is right now; zero outside a page render.

methods.name: setPendingElements
methods.doc: A dynamic block claims its element class before rendering, so a block that renders nothing still counts.

methods.name: takePendingElements

methods.name: recordElementRule

methods.name: elementRules

methods.name: recordGallery

methods.name: galleries

methods.name: reset

Renders a block tree the way the reference renders post_content:
delimiters gone, each block's own HTML kept with inner blocks rendered
in place, then the per-block render-time additions (layout classes, the
paragraph class, image attributes, gallery ids, style-variation
counters), and finally texturize over the whole.

Style variations that carry a numbered companion class at render.
These come from the active theme's registered block styles; the set
mirrors the reference's theme until the engine reads theme data.

Shared wording for `wp plugin update` and `wp theme update`. Captured

stdout when nothing changed). `--exclude` always prints the skipped

classes.name: Minn\Cli\CacheCommand
classes.doc: `wp cache flush`: the engine has no object cache, so this is a no-op success.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc:
Flushes the object cache.

The engine does not run an object cache. The verb still succeeds so
fleet scripts that call it after a write do not abort.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Commands
classes.doc:
The verbs the engine answers to. Every one is registered for the
before_wp_load phase, which WP-CLI runs before it looks for WordPress,
and each replaces the bundled subcommand of the same name (a deferred
addition lands after the bundle and overrides its leaf).

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers every engine verb with WP-CLI in the phase it runs in.

methods.name: leaf
methods.doc:
Registers a leaf and re-adds it after the parent lands. WP-CLI
registers `plugin` as a namespace first; its later class command
would otherwise overwrite our list.

methods.name: replace
methods.doc:
A root command the bundle also registers. Re-add after the bundle
without recursing into our own after_add_command hook.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\DirectorySearch
classes.doc:
Shared wording for `wp theme search` and `wp plugin search`. The
default table is name/slug/rating; Success prints before the rows and
only for table/yaml. json/csv/count print the Formatter output alone.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Searches wordpress.org for one kind of asset and prints the page.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Installer
classes.doc:
The swap, both ways. Install parks WordPress's own files beside the
webroot, lays the engine and its shape files down, and leaves
wp-config.php and wp-content untouched; eject puts every parked file
back and removes what install wrote. A manifest in minn/.install.json
is the record eject works from. Preflight says what the site will and
will not get before anything moves.

constants.name: CORE_ENTRIES
constants.doc: The files WordPress keeps at the webroot, moved aside as a set.

constants.name: WRITTEN_TREES
constants.doc: Webroot trees install writes (shape files + require placeholders) and eject deletes before restoring the park.

constants.name: LEGACY_PUBLISHED
constants.doc:
Leftover webroot copies from an earlier installer that published
assets outside minn/. Eject still deletes them.

constants.name: SKIP
constants.doc: Development-only trees inside the engine or the admin bundle that never ship.

methods.name: main
methods.doc: The bin entry: runs one command against a webroot and returns the exit code.

methods.name: preflight
methods.doc: What the site will and will not get; the worst light decides install. The report lands in the output.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Prints what the webroot is running.

methods.name: install
methods.doc: Installs the engine into a webroot when the preflight allows it.

methods.name: eject
methods.doc: Puts WordPress back and removes the engine's files.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: What a webroot is running: minn, wordpress, or unknown.

methods.name: writePlaceholders
methods.doc:
Empty PHP files for every wp-includes/*.php and wp-admin/includes/*.php
the reference has, so a plugin `require ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/plugin.php'`
resolves. The engine already provides the symbols; the file is the contract.

methods.name: move
methods.doc: rename() first; copy+remove when the park is on another filesystem.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\MaintenanceCommand
classes.doc:
`wp maintenance-mode`: the `.maintenance` marker in the webroot. The
engine does not take the public site down while the file is present;
fleet scripts still need the verb to succeed so an update can bookend
itself with activate/deactivate.

methods.name: activate
methods.doc: Activates maintenance mode.

methods.name: deactivate
methods.doc: Deactivates maintenance mode.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Displays maintenance mode status.

methods.name: is_active
methods.doc: Detects maintenance mode status. Exit 0 when active, 1 when not.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\MinnCommand
classes.doc:
Identifies the engine.

## EXAMPLES

wp minn version
wp minn info
wp minn probe

methods.name: version
methods.doc: Prints the engine version.

methods.name: probe
methods.doc:
Prints the inventory CaptainCore gathers from inside WordPress:
plugins, themes, must-use plugins, core version, home. One
`key:value` line per field; JSON values have no newlines. Split
on the first colon only.

methods.name: info
methods.doc: Prints the engine's version and where it runs from.

methods.name: cron
methods.doc: Runs the engine's scheduled work: due posts go live, expired rows are swept.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
Sends a test email through the site's mail settings.

## OPTIONS

<to>
: The address to send to.

methods.name: preflight
methods.doc:
Says what a WordPress webroot will and will not get from the engine.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot to inspect. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Parks WordPress and installs the engine into a webroot.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

[--park=<dir>]
: Where WordPress's own files go. Defaults to wp-parked beside the webroot.

[--force]
: Install even when preflight is RED.

methods.name: eject
methods.doc:
Removes the engine and puts WordPress's files back.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: status
methods.doc:
Says whether a webroot runs WordPress or the engine.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: scripts
methods.doc:
The site's script pack: the GPL `wp-*` JavaScript packages the engine
does not reimplement, which a few plugin front ends need (the
WooCommerce block cart and checkout). The engine never ships them;
this installs them into the site's own wp-content, from the
WordPress the swap parked beside the webroot, or from any WordPress
tree named with --from.

## OPTIONS

[<action>]
: status (the default), install, or remove.

[--from=<path>]
: A WordPress tree to take the packages from. Defaults to the parked
copy the install recorded.

methods.name: recovery
methods.doc:
The extensions recovery paused after they killed a request, and the
way back. A plugin or theme that fatals is paused so the next
request answers without it; nothing loads it again until it is
resumed here.

## OPTIONS

[<action>]
: status (the default), resume, or resume-all.

[<name>]
: For resume: the plugin file or theme slug to let back in.

[--theme]
: Treat the name as a theme rather than a plugin.

methods.name: parkedTree
methods.doc: The WordPress the swap parked beside this webroot, when the manifest names one.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\OptionCommand
classes.doc:
Options, read and written straight to the options table. Serialized
values are decoded by the engine's own reader, and arrays written back
in the stored form.

methods.name: get

Gets the value for an option.

## OPTIONS

<key>
: Key for the option.

[--format=<format>]
: Get value in a particular format.
---
default: var_export
options:
- var_export
- json
- yaml
---

methods.doc:
Adds a new option value.

## OPTIONS

<key>
: The name of the option to add.

[<value>]
: The value of the option to add. If omitted, the value is read from STDIN.

[--format=<format>]
: The serialization format for the value.
---
default: plaintext
options:
- plaintext
- json
---

[--autoload=<autoload>]

---
options:
- 'on'
- 'off'
---

methods.doc:
Updates an option value.

<key>

[<value>]

[--autoload=<autoload>]

---
options:
- 'on'

---

[--format=<format>]

---
default: plaintext
options:

methods.doc:
Deletes an option.

<key>...
: Key for the option.

methods.doc: The value argument, or STDIN when omitted; JSON decoded when asked.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: A stored value as PHP data: serialized blobs decoded, anything else as the string it is.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\PluginCommand
classes.doc: `wp plugin list|install|update|activate|deactivate|delete`: the inventory and the fleet's install/update/delete.

methods.name: list
methods.doc:
Lists installed plugins, must-use plugins, and drop-ins.

## OPTIONS

[--status=<status>]
: Filter to one status: active, inactive, must-use, or dropin.

[--field=<field>]
: Prints the value of a single field for each plugin.

[--fields=<fields>]
: Limit the output to specific object fields.

[--format=<format>]
: Render output in a particular format.
---
default: table
options:
- table
- csv
- json
- count
- yaml
---

methods.name: activate
methods.doc:
Activates one or more plugins: a WordPress plugin joins active_plugins
(its stored state; the engine runs none of its code), a Minn extension
joins the engine's own list.

## OPTIONS

<plugin>...
: One or more plugins to activate.

methods.name: deactivate
methods.doc:
Deactivates one or more plugins.

## OPTIONS

<plugin>...
: One or more plugins to deactivate.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Installs one or more plugins from wordpress.org, a zip, or a URL.

## OPTIONS

<plugin|zip|url>...
: A plugin slug, a local zip path, or a zip URL.

[--version=<version>]
: Install that wordpress.org version instead of the current one.

[--force]
: Overwrite an installed copy of the same folder.

[--activate]
: Activate the plugin after it is installed (or if it is already on disk).

classes.name: Minn\Content\Excerpt
classes.doc:
The reference's generated excerpt, as captured from probe posts: - Only text-bearing blocks contribute. Containers (group, columns, column, media-text) pass their allowed children through; anything not on the list vanishes with everything inside it (code, details, buttons, images, galleries, covers, dynamic blocks, and the nested list-item, so a modern list contributes nothing while a classic one does). - The text stops at the first (in a feed it runs on). - Block-level tags read as spaces; inline tags (and
) read as nothing. - Whitespace collapses, 55 words, an ellipsis when cut, wrapped in

, texturized (a feed texturizes first, so its inline code stays raw). A hand-written excerpt skips the block filter.

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
The more tag ends a listing's excerpt but not a feed's, and a feed
texturizes before the tags go (so inline code keeps straight quotes)
where a listing texturizes the finished text.

methods.name: forFeed
methods.doc:
The excerpt as a feed carries it: the whole content counts (no stop at
the more tag), texturize runs before the tags are stripped, and the
paragraph is not texturized again.

methods.name: source
methods.doc: The stored excerpt, or the content's allowed markup.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: The first 55 words with tags gone, an ellipsis when cut, empty for none.

methods.name: recordRendered
methods.doc:
A generated excerpt drops the disallowed blocks first and renders the
rest before trimming, so the allowed blocks count as rendered on the
page: the stylesheet prints their block styles even when nothing of
theirs survives the trim.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Manifest
classes.doc:
minn.json, read as data. A folder under wp-content/plugins (or
mu-plugins) with this file is an extension; the same folder may also be
a WordPress plugin, in which case the two share a name and a version.

{
"name": "Block Visibility for Minn",
"version": "1.0.0",
"license": "MIT",
"replaces": ["block-visibility/block-visibility.php"],
"autoload": {"Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\": "src/"},
"extension": "Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\Extension",
"shortcodes": ["example_tag"],
"blocks": ["vendor/block"],
"types": [{"slug": "zz_note", "name": "Notes", "rest_base": "zz-note"}]
}

"replaces" names the WordPress plugin files whose behaviour this
extension stands in for; the extension is active whenever one of them is
in active_plugins, or when its own folder is listed there, or when it is
named in the minn_active_extensions option. "shortcodes" and "blocks"
are the content tokens preflight treats as provided instead of missing.
"types" are extra post types the engine should serve on wp/v2.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Resolver
classes.doc:
Turns a public URL into a Resolution, following the reference's observed
rules:

- Unpaged content and archives without a trailing slash redirect to the
slashed form, as typed (case kept); paged views, search, and 404s do not.
- Query-var forms (?p=, ?page_id=, ?cat=, ?tag=, ?author=, ?m=, ?name=,
?pagename=) redirect to the pretty form when the target is public.
- Archive-shaped paths (category, tag, author, search, a four-digit year)
are strict: a mismatch is a 404 with no guessing.
- Plain-segment paths try the page hierarchy, then the post structure,
then redirect to the closest published page or post whose name starts
with the last segment, pages before posts, newest first.
- Empty term and date archives are 404; an author archive is 200 for any
name, even one that belongs to nobody.
- Non-public posts are 404 to anonymous readers and served to a reader
who can edit them.

What the public sees when the engine cannot answer: a plain page with no
detail, while the detail goes to the log. Installed once per request,
it turns display_errors off (unless the site's own WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY asks
for them) and catches the fatal errors PHP would otherwise print.

methods.doc:
Opens the window in which a failure is an extension's fault: while
the plugins and the theme's functions file load and the boot actions
fire, code that fails fails for every visitor, so pausing it heals
the site. A failure after that (a route, a shortcode, a template)
answers to one request's input and is never grounds for a pause;
it is logged and the request ends in the error page.

methods.doc:
What to do with a fatal beyond showing the page: the engine records
the extension it came from so the next request loads without it.
Installed once the runtime is up, since it needs the database.

methods.doc:

errors. Only ever reached when WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY (or WP_DEBUG) is on:
a site that has not asked never learns this much from a response.

methods.doc: Whatever a half-finished render left in the output buffers goes; the error page must stand alone.

methods.doc:

take the request down: a site that cannot record a pause should
still answer with the error page.

classes.doc:
What a route requires of its caller, as data on the route: the router
enforces it before the handler runs, so a grep over the attributes is
the authorization surface. The two refusals are the reference's: a
caller who is not signed in gets the sign-in code (401), a signed-in
caller who lacks the capability gets the refusal code (403); how a bad
nonce is answered belongs to whoever judges the policy.

argument allows: `policy: new Policy(Access::Cap, 'upload_files',
refuse: 'rest_cannot_create', message: '...')`.

lost-password and reset flows, and logout all live there and link there.

uptime probes, scripted sign-ins) and answers in place with the same
shapes; a bare GET of it sends a browser to the clean page. Sessions
and cookies validate on the engine AND on WordPress either way.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Canvas

One GD bitmap and the operations the media layer needs on it. Every
operation returns a new canvas; alpha is preserved throughout, which is
what makes PNG and WebP sub-sizes match the reference's.

methods.name: open
methods.doc:
A canvas from an image file, or null when it cannot be decoded or
would not fit in memory. The header names the dimensions before a
pixel is decoded, so a small file that claims a huge canvas is
refused instead of taking the request down.

methods.name: resample
methods.doc: Resamples a source box onto a destination box.
shapes: @param array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int} $box dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h (the GD argument order)

params.name: box
params.shape: array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int}

methods.name: crop

methods.doc: A canvas cut to a rectangle, resized to a target when given.

methods.name: rotate
methods.doc: A canvas turned by an angle, or null when GD refuses.

methods.name: flipVertical
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored on either axis.

methods.name: flipHorizontal
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored left to right.

methods.name: copy
methods.doc: An untouched copy of the canvas.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Writes the bitmap in the given format; the directory is created when missing.

methods.name: stream
methods.doc: Writes the image to the output in a format, at a quality.

methods.name: affordable
methods.doc:
Whether a bitmap of these dimensions fits the memory left to this
request: five bytes a pixel for the decoded image (GD keeps four and
a little), twice over because every operation makes a second canvas,
under what memory_limit leaves after what is already in use.

methods.name: memoryLimit
methods.doc: memory_limit in bytes, or null when it is unlimited.

classes.doc:
The classic `[gallery]` shortcode's markup. Every gallery on a page is
numbered from one shared per-request counter, and the wrapper names both
that number and the post the gallery sits in, so two galleries on one page
can be styled apart.

The single quotes around the wrapper attributes and the tab-indented item
body are the reference's, and themes have styled against them for long
enough that they are contract rather than formatting.

candidates an image's sizes yield. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/media.json.

The largest box inside the limits that keeps the ratio: only sides over
their limit shrink, the smaller ratio wins, and a result one pixel short

classes.name: Minn\Media\Upload
classes.doc:
One file arriving for the library, on either transport: a multipart
field named "file" (a temporary upload to move) or a raw body whose
Content-Disposition names the file. The parent is read from the same
request, wherever the client put it.

The image type the bytes themselves say they are, or null when they
are not an image the library knows. What the name claims is checked
against this: the reference refuses non-image bytes under an image
name and renames a file whose bytes are a different image type.

methods.doc: The same upload under a name whose extension matches a mime type.

methods.doc: Whether the file is an image the engine will make sizes for; SVG is not.

A safe file name: one extension. Every dot-separated part between the
base and the last extension that is not itself an allowed extension
is joined with an underscore, so "shell.php.png" lands as
"shell_php.png" and no handler can be talked into running it.

The writes the media library makes. An Upload becomes an attachment: the
file lands in the dated uploads directory under a unique name, the row is
inserted with the stored name as its title and slug, and an image gets
its sub-sizes and the serialized metadata blob. Edits stamp the row
modified; removal takes the files with the row.

classes.name: Minn\Query\DateSql
classes.doc:
The WHERE fragment of a date query in the reference's shape: before and
after bounds as full datetimes (inclusive bounds close the day), the
date parts as MySQL functions compared or listed, groups joined by
their relation, columns validated against the known date columns.

shapes: @param array<string, string> $tables table key to prefixed table name

params.name: tables
params.doc: table key to prefixed table name

methods.doc: Sanitises to the reference's shape: every level carries column, compare and relation.

methods.name: isFirstOrder
methods.doc: Whether a date query is one clause rather than a group of them.

methods.doc: A column name as "table.column", the default for anything unknown.

methods.doc: The WHERE fragment for a date query.

methods.doc: A full datetime from a string or a parts array; a parts array rounds up to the end of its unit when asked.

classes.name: Minn\Query\MetaSql
classes.doc:
The JOIN and WHERE fragments of a meta query in the reference's shape:
one meta-table join per clause (the first under the table's own name,
then mt1, mt2, ...), INNER joins unless an OR relation or a NOT EXISTS
clause needs LEFT ones, and casts by the clause's declared type. Under
an OR relation a clause shares an equality-shaped sibling's join.

shapes: @param array<string, array{0: string, 1: string}> $tables meta type to [table, object column]

methods.doc:
Normalises a raw meta_query: clauses get key/value/compare/type
defaults, a nested group its relation, and a "relation" key sits on
every level. Named clauses keep their names.

methods.name: isFirstOrder
methods.doc: A clause rather than a group: it names a key or a value.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: The JOIN and WHERE fragments for a meta query.

methods.doc: The clauses the last build resolved, by name.
shapes: @return array<string, array{alias: string, cast: string}> clauses seen while building, by name or alias

methods.doc: Whether any level of the query relates its clauses by OR.

methods.doc: The CAST target for a clause type; CHAR means no cast.

methods.name: hasOrWithNotExists

methods.name: values

Who is making this REST call. Resolved once from the cookie and nonce;
an anonymous or failed caller has id 0 and every capability check fails.

methods.name: resolveAs
methods.doc:
Settles the caller as a session already proven elsewhere: an
in-process request a plugin makes through rest_do_request() carries
no nonce, so it runs as whoever the outer request resolved.

methods.name: session
methods.doc: The session, or null for an anonymous or refused caller.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The caller's user id, 0 when anonymous.

methods.name: can
methods.doc: Whether the caller holds a capability, on a post when given.

methods.name: capabilities
methods.doc: The capability engine.

methods.name: require
methods.signature: require(string $code = 'rest_not_logged_in', string $message = 'You are not currently logged in.', int $status = 401): Minn\Auth\Authenticated
methods.doc:
The session, or the reference's refusal: a bad nonce is always 403
rest_cookie_invalid_nonce; no identity is the caller-supplied error.

methods.name: requireFloor
methods.doc:
The floor every Minn Admin route shares: a signed-in caller who can
edit posts, plus any further capability named, all refused with the
same rest_forbidden the reference uses. Returns the caller's id.

methods.name: requireCap
methods.doc: 403 rest_forbidden unless the caller holds every capability named.

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: 401 for an anonymous caller, 403 for one who is signed in but refused.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Embed
classes.doc:
The _embed decoration and the embed context. Every embeddable link in an
object's _links is answered in-process as the same caller with
context=embed and placed under _embedded[rel]; a rel whose every embed
came back empty or as an error is left out, while an empty list beside a
full one stays (wp:term keeps its empty tags list next to the categories).
Lists have _fields applied per item before the links are read, so a
_fields value without _links embeds nothing there; a single object embeds
first and is filtered afterwards. The embed context is the view object
cut to the reference's key set for that kind of item.

constants.name: KEYS
constants.value: array (   'post' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'date',     2 => 'slug',     3 => 'type',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'title',     6 => 'excerpt',     7 => 'author',     8 => 'featured_media',     9 => '_links',   ),   'media' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'date',     2 => 'slug',     3 => 'type',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'title',     6 => 'author',     7 => 'featured_media',     8 => 'caption',     9 => 'alt_text',     10 => 'media_type',     11 => 'mime_type',     12 => 'media_details',     13 => 'source_url',     14 => '_links',   ),   'user' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'name',     2 => 'url',     3 => 'description',     4 => 'link',     5 => 'slug',     6 => 'avatar_urls',     7 => '_links',   ),   'term' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'link',     2 => 'name',     3 => 'slug',     4 => 'taxonomy',     5 => '_links',   ),   'comment' =>    array (     0 => 'id',     1 => 'parent',     2 => 'author',     3 => 'author_name',     4 => 'author_url',     5 => 'date',     6 => 'content',     7 => 'link',     8 => 'type',     9 => 'author_avatar_urls',     10 => '_links',   ), )

methods.name: requested
methods.doc: Null when _embed is absent; [] for every rel; otherwise the rels asked for. @return ?list<string>

methods.name: decorate
methods.doc: Decorates a finished response: the embed context, then _embedded, then the deferred _fields.

methods.name: answer
methods.doc: The linked object in embed context, or null when the link answers with an error.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: A REST href in either URL form, as the route path and its query. @return array{0: string, 1: array<string, string>}

methods.name: kind
methods.doc: Which key set a route's objects take in embed context; null for routes without one.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\EngineRoutes
classes.doc:
The engine's own REST routes in the reference's regex form, for the
index and for the runtime's server, whose route table plugin code reads
to learn what the site answers (a missing /wp/v2/comments there reads as
"comments are off").

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The router's routes as route => methods, the way the index lists them.

methods.name: forms
methods.doc:
A route attribute pattern as the reference writes routes: `{id:\d+}`
becomes `(?P<id>\d+)`, a bare capture matches one segment, a `{rest*}`
capture the remainder, and an alternation of literals expands to one
route per literal.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Fields
classes.doc:
The _fields response filter. Dot paths descend ("title.rendered"); the
object's own key order is kept. Applied per item on list responses and to
the whole payload otherwise, which is why _fields on the associative
types response strips every key and yields [] over HTTP, a reference
quirk the engine reproduces by construction.

constructor.doc: embedded first and filtered by Embed afterwards

params.name: deferred
params.doc: true when _embed rides along: a single object is

methods.name: fromQuery
methods.doc: The _fields selection a query carries, or null for everything.

methods.name: withLinksForEmbedded
methods.doc: The same paths plus _links whenever _embedded is among them: the reference's single-object rule under _embed.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: The object with only the selected fields.

methods.name: select
methods.doc:
The fields a response keeps when a caller names some: known fields as
given, dotted paths whose root is known, and `id` whenever it exists.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\GlobalStylesController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/global-styles: the site editor's saved styles (one post per
theme, read and written by id, with its revisions) and the active
theme's own styles and variations. There is no collection, no create
and no delete; the post is made on first use, as on the reference.

constants.name: CANNOT_EDIT
constants.value: 'Sorry, you are not allowed to edit this global style.'

constants.name: CANNOT_READ_REVISIONS
constants.value: 'Sorry, you are not allowed to view revisions of this post.'

methods.name: single
methods.doc: The saved styles by id: anyone who edits posts may read them, editing context needs the theme.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Replaces the title, settings, or styles the body names; what it leaves out stays.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The active theme's settings and styles, the engine's defaults underneath.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc: The style variations the active theme ships.

methods.name: revisions
methods.doc: The revisions of the saved styles, newest first; all of them unless per_page pages them.

methods.name: revision
methods.doc: One revision of the saved styles.

methods.name: requireTheme
methods.doc: The theme routes answer only for the active stylesheet, and only to those who edit posts.

methods.name: requireParent
methods.doc: Revisions are for those who edit the theme, of a parent that is a global-styles post.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: A title arrives as a string or as {raw}; anything else is ignored.

methods.name: node
methods.doc: settings and styles are objects when present; a scalar is the reference's type error, null is ignored.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\GlobalStylesObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2/global-styles item, theme, and revision shapes.

methods.name: item
methods.doc:
The saved styles: the title both ways, settings by origin, styles
with their presets resolved, the links; in editing context the
app's lock fields too, which a global-styles post never carries.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The active theme's own styles as the themes/{stylesheet} route answers them.

methods.name: revision
methods.doc:
One revision row: both nodes when the body holds anything at all,
neither when it is blank, then the row's own facts; no links.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: Writing methods appear for a theme editor; the CSS action for whoever may write CSS.

methods.name: node
methods.doc: An empty node is an object on the wire, never a list.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\ListQuery
classes.doc:
The collection parameters a wp/v2 list accepts, read once from the
request into typed fields: the page, the id lists, the slugs, the search
words, and the ordering. clauses() turns the narrowing ones into the SQL
fragments and parameters a controller appends to its own visibility
clause, so posts, pages, and media build their lists the same way.

constructor.signature: __construct(int $page = 1, int $perPage = 10, array $include = array ( ), array $exclude = array ( ), array $author = array ( ), array $authorExclude = array ( ), array $parent = array ( ), array $parentExclude = array ( ), array $slugs = array ( ), array $words = array ( ), ?int $menuOrder = NULL, string $orderBy = 'date', string $order = 'DESC', array $terms = array ( ), array $termsExclude = array ( ))

methods.doc: The list parameters read from the request.

The narrowing clauses, each starting with " AND", and their parameters

methods.doc: The first row of the requested page.

methods.name: idsWithZero

post=0 means "no post".

classes.name: Minn\Rest\ParamCheck

The required / validate / sanitize pass over a request's declared arguments.

hands them in already normalised to true, false, or [message, details].

wp/v2 plugins: what sits in wp-content/plugins, in the reference's
shape. Minn extensions (a minn.json manifest) are listed alongside the
WordPress plugins the folder still holds; the engine runs the former
and only records the latter's stored state. Activation writes the same
options the reference and the extension loader read; files are never
installed or deleted from here.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PolicyGate
classes.doc:
Judges a route's policy against the caller, with the reference's
refusals: a caller who is not signed in gets the policy's sign-in code
at 401, a bad nonce is always 403 rest_cookie_invalid_nonce, and a
signed-in caller who lacks a capability gets the refusal code at 403.
The edit-context policy is judged as well when the request asks for it.

methods.name: closure
methods.doc: The judge as the router takes it.

methods.name: judge
methods.doc: Throws the refusal the policy names, or returns.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostObject
classes.doc:
Builds the wp/v2 post and page objects in the reference's shape: the
view context, the edit context (raw+rendered dual fields, editor-only
fields, and cap-gated wp:action-* links), and their _links blocks.

constants.name: NAVIGATION
constants.doc: The one post type whose REST shape is not post-shaped.

constants.name: BLOCK
constants.doc: The other: a pattern carries its content raw, its category, and its sync status.

methods.name: restBase
methods.doc: The rest_base of a type.

methods.name: view
methods.doc: The view-context object: the shared fields, then the type's own, then class_list and _links.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: The _links of a post in the view context.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc:
The edit-context object for a given caller: raw+rendered dual fields,
password, permalink_template, generated_slug, block_version, Minn
Admin's registered list fields, and the cap-gated action links.

methods.name: permalinkTemplate
methods.doc:
The editor's sample permalink: the structure with the name token left
in place (pages: the parent path plus %pagename%), or the query form
when permalinks are plain.

methods.name: modifiedUnsaved
methods.doc: Whether a live post carries an autosave newer than its saved revision.

methods.name: lockHolder
methods.doc: The OTHER user holding a live _edit_lock (150 second window), or null.

methods.name: editLinks
methods.doc: The view links plus the caller's verbs and cap-gated wp:action-* entries.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: A MySQL datetime in the reference's ISO form.

methods.name: navigationView
methods.doc:
A navigation menu is a post with almost nothing on it: no author, no
excerpt, no featured image, no comments, no taxonomies, and so no
class list either. What it does carry is a template field and the
rendered menu.

methods.name: blockView
methods.doc:
A pattern (wp_block) is read by editors only, so its title and
content come raw even in view context: no rendered title, no rendered
content. It carries an excerpt, the footnotes meta, its pattern
categories, and the sync status core registers beside meta.

methods.name: viewTerms
methods.doc:
The taxonomies a non-page carries, each as [term_id, slug] pairs; the
format terms only for posts.

methods.name: typeFields
methods.doc:
Pages carry parent and menu_order first; posts carry their term ids,
and only the post type has sticky and format.

methods.name: classList
methods.doc:
The reference's class_list order: identity, type, status, format (posts
only), password, thumbnail, hentry, then one class per term.

methods.name: termLinks
methods.doc: The taxonomy links a type carries: posts their categories and tags, patterns their pattern categories, pages and menus none.

methods.name: allow
methods.doc:
What the caller may do to this post, which the reference reports in
every context: a reader sees GET, an editor of the post sees the
write verbs, and DELETE only when they may delete it too.

methods.name: gmt
methods.doc:
A gmt timestamp for the wire: the stored one, or, when it is the
draft zero, the local time converted through the site's offset, the
way the reference derives it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockHooks
classes.doc:
The Block Hooks API on the engine's own front end: a plugin asks for its
block to be inserted next to an anchor block in a template part or a
pattern (WooCommerce puts the mini-cart after the navigation in a
header), and the markup the renderer reads carries those insertions.

The facade owns the traversal (wp-api/blocks.php); this is the seam the
theme blocks call, and it stays inert until a plugin actually hooks
something, so a site without such a plugin parses nothing extra.

methods.doc: Whether block hooks are registered and the runtime is up.

methods.name: forPart
methods.doc:
A template part's markup with its hooked blocks inserted. The context
is the part itself: a plugin reads its area to tell a header from a
footer, and its content to see whether its block is already there.

methods.name: registeredPattern
methods.doc:
A plugin-registered pattern's content, hooks already applied by the
registry, for a slug the theme does not carry. Null when the runtime
is not up or nothing registered that name.

methods.name: forPattern
methods.doc:
A theme pattern's markup with its hooked blocks inserted, with the
pattern array as the context (blockTypes and categories are how a
plugin recognises a header pattern).

A block widget's legacy class name. Every widget the block editor saves
is one block of markup, and a classic theme styles it by the widget
class the equivalent legacy widget used, so the wrapper carries a
second class named after the FIRST block in the content. A block with
no legacy equivalent adds nothing.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentCloser
classes.doc:
The Discussion setting that closes comments on old posts. Observed on the
reference: only the "post" type closes (the types filter changes nothing),
status is not consulted, the age is whole days on post_date_gmt and must
exceed the setting (a fifteen-day-old post stays open at fifteen), and zero
days switches the rule off.

methods.doc: Whether comments stay open on a post under the close-after-days setting.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Hooks
classes.doc:
The hook registry plugin code registers into and the engine fires.
Semantics come from contracts/fixtures/api/hooks.json: callbacks run
by ascending priority then insertion order; a callback added at a
higher priority during a run takes part in that run, one added at the
current or a lower priority waits for the next; a callback removed
before its turn is skipped; the "all" hook sees every firing with the
hook name first and every argument regardless of its accepted count.

methods.doc: Called with each hook name the first time a callback registers under it.

methods.doc: The live registry, for a hook object to share by reference.

methods.doc: The priority a running hook is at, or false when it is idle.

mu-plugins first, then active_plugins in stored order, each file
included once. A plugin loads only when the static symbol read finds
nothing the runtime lacks; otherwise it is reported and skipped so the
site keeps rendering. The lifecycle actions fire between the phases.

constants.name: MINN_ADMIN
constants.doc:
Minn Admin loads as code for its adapters (surfaces, licenses,
connectors, custom CSS, the plugin routes the engine has no
controller for), but the engine owns the shell, the front bar, the
sign-in flow, and maintenance: those hooks come off right after the

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Recovery
classes.doc:
Recovery from a fatal in someone else's code. When a plugin or theme
kills the boot of a request, the file it died in names it; a second
such failure inside ten minutes records it as paused, and the next
request loads without it: the site comes back on its own instead of
staying down until a human reads the log. One failure is only noted:
a pause is a site-wide decision, and a single request can be a
crafted one. Failures after boot (a route, a template) never pause
anything; see Failure::armRecovery().

The paused list is stored where WordPress stores it, in the same shape
(`paused_plugins` keyed by plugin file, `paused_themes` by stylesheet,
each holding type, file, line and message), so a site that ejects back
to WordPress finds the pause it left with. The strikes live in the
engine's own `minn_recovery_strikes` option.

fault and pausing something would not fix it. A symlinked plugin
reports its real location; the realpath map (real folder to the
folder under plugins/) brings it home first.

methods.doc:

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ScriptPack
classes.doc:
The site-supplied script pack: the `wp-*` JavaScript packages the engine
does not reimplement, which a few plugins' front ends need (WooCommerce's
block cart and checkout are the reason it exists).

These packages are GPL, so the engine never ships them: the SITE installs
them into its own `wp-content`, the way it installs a language pack, and
the engine registers the handles only when they are actually there. A
site owner adding GPL files to a site that already runs GPL plugins is
not the engine distributing GPL; nothing under `minn/` changes.

The engine's own MIT packages under `minn/assets/wp` always win: the pack
fills the gaps around them, it does not replace them.
